title: The Shadow Laughs

evidence.note: Published 1933, so public domain would rest on a missing notice or a missing renewal. The 1933 print's 28th-year renewal window is 1960-1961. The Internet Archive pages for the two Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes were opened and their titles checked: Third Series, Parts 12-13, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, Jan-Dec 1960 (Vol 14 No 1-2) and Jan-Dec 1961 (Vol 15 No 1-2). I did not read the entries inside them or search the Copyright Office catalog, so I make no claim that no renewal exists. Both volumes still need a hand check for the title.

editorial:
The Shadow Laughs is a 1933 American pre-Code mystery film directed by Arthur Hoerl for Trojan Pictures. Wikipedia lists Hal Skelly, Rose Hobart and Harry T. Morey as its stars, and gives a release date of March 27, 1933. The Internet Archive description calls it Cesar Romero's film debut and centers on Skelly as a newspaper reporter. A creator might want it as a low-budget pre-Code curiosity, or for the Romero debut.

The rights trap is the print itself. A film published in 1933 is only free if its renewal was never filed, and this dossier has not confirmed that either way. The Internet Archive copy is incomplete, so a reuser should also check where any other copy came from. The Internet Archive description says the film is not related to the radio series and comic book character The Shadow.
faq: Can I reuse The Shadow Laughs (1933) freely?

Not yet. Whether the 1933 print is free depends on whether a renewal was filed in 1960 or 1961, and that is unconfirmed. Check the Copyright Office records and the 1960 and 1961 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes first.
Is the Internet Archive copy complete?
No. Its description says four minutes are missing, including the title card and opening credits.
